title: How OpenAI Built ChatGPT for Bankers and Analysts — Joseph Kim, OpenAI
talk_summary: Joseph Kim describes ChatGPT for financial services, built largely on the same plugin/MCP/skills platform available to outside developers, with licensed data hosted and indexed in-house rather than relying on third-party MCP connectors. The transferable content is mostly about product experience and data/tool plumbing (templates, citation viewers, MCP apps, skills) plus a framing of 'unhobbling' via persistent agents; there are no agent-orchestration, review, or cost techniques with hard numbers.

takeaways.technique: Host and index your own data behind MCP instead of trusting third-party connectors
takeaways.what_they_do: They evaluated existing MCP connectors for financial data, found latency/error/search-quality problems, licensed the data directly, and built their own hosting and search indices, while still exposing it to the model over MCP.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We looked at existing MCP connectors for financial data and found that many had issues with latency, errors, or search quality.

takeaways.technique: Firm-specific templates as a first-class artifact layer
takeaways.what_they_do: A template system injects the organization's approved spreadsheet/presentation templates so model output is already in the firm's format, reducing post-processing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We built a template system that gives users access to the firm's approved templates when generating spreadsheets and presentations.

takeaways.technique: Citation/source inspection as part of the review surface
takeaways.what_they_do: Citation viewers let the user open the exact source passage or table behind a number, making verification a natural step rather than a separate audit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we built citation viewers that let people inspect the source passages and tables in behind an answer

takeaways.technique: Persistent goal-holding agents instead of prompt-per-turn
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue the next 'unhobbling' step is agents that hold a goal, retain relevant context, and keep working in the background after a direction is given, rather than requiring a new prompt each step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A persistent agent can hold on to a goal, remember the relevant context, and continue working in the background.

takeaways.technique: Compaction and sparse attention for long context
takeaways.what_they_do: They cite sparse attention and compaction as the techniques that resolved context-window limits, implying long work is handled by compacting rather than by ever-larger windows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We've also solved concerns around things like context window length using things like sparse attention and compaction.

takeaways.what_they_do: They define a per-task threshold where review cost drops below time saved, and advise building the review/approval interface before the model crosses it so delegation is ready.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Below that threshold, improvements can be hard to appreciate... if checking and fixing its work still takes as long as doing it yourself
